neighborhood_overview:
The apartment is in a classic pre-war East Village brick apartment building, originally built for working-class Ukranian immigrants who formed the neighborhood in the 1800s. The cheap rents attracted the Beatniks in the 1950s, hippies in the '60s and punk rockers in the '80s. The neighborhood became the center of New York's counterculture and is still more affordable than the West Village. description:
Charming single-family home on a safe, quiet, tree lined block in Bay Ridge, Brooklyn. The house is furnished in a mid century modern style. Upstairs there is a large master bedroom with wonderful light. There is also a second bedroom facing the backyard and a small office that can be turned into a third bedroom if necessary. Downstairs is the eat in kitchen, living room and bathroom. Best of all, out back there is a huge garden with a patio area - perfect for BBQing, or unwinding in a hammock.

The space
Our home is a wood frame house built in 1921. Not too many of these types of homes are still around. It's been my pleasure to give this home a comfortable mid century modern vibe. It has an open and decluttered feel. Both the kitchen and the bathroom have been updated without destroying what was already there - such as the old tiles in the bathroom and the midcentury laminate counter top in the kitchen. Hence, the spirit and feel of the old house still remains. <
neighborhood_overview:
Bay Ridge is well known for its warm, relaxed neighborhood feel and pretty residential blocks that have stayed pretty much the same since the 20s and 30s. Bay Ridge is also a very diverse neighborhood. It has a mix of Chinese, Muslim, Polish, Italian and Scandinavian immigrants all peacefully coexisting. As a result the dining options are as varied as dim sum and falafel to pizza and kielbasa. This is also a waterfront community with ferry service available to get into the city or out to the beach.

Five min. from our house is Mc Kinley Park. Here you can enjoy large trees, grass, a playground for children and sprinklers. A bus ride away, in Sunset Park, there is an olympic size pool. We also have a local movie theatre: Alpine Cinema, where you can catch the latest movie, walking distance from our house. Carroll Gardens takes its name from the large front gardens that many homes feature often full of roses, St. Francis statuary and elaborate holiday decorations.

Carroll Gardens is at once the heart of old school Brooklyn and the height of brownstone Brooklyn’s boom. The neighborhood has long been known for its red sauce joints, lively street life and old timers hanging out on stoops. But now neighborhood staples like Caputo’s Bakery and Monteleone’s Café abut upscale stroller shops, yoga studios and fro-yo joints. Despite the newcomers, the neighborhood still feels like a small town, one of the few places where you know your neighbors, your postman and your grocer by name.

You’ll find no air of pretension or exclusivity in Carroll Gardens. It’s a lovely neighborhood full of familiarity and family life.

On Court Street, you’ll find kids zooming around on scooters, new moms with strollers and neighborhood grandmas pushing shopping carts.

description:
Renovated and sunny duplex with deck and shaded yard in hip and family friendly Clinton Hill, Brooklyn

The space
This renovated duplex in Clinton Hill, Brooklyn occupies the bottom two floors of a 3-story townhouse built at the turn of the 19th Century. The bright open-plan living, kitchen and dining area is on one floor and has large windows, an exposed brick wall, exposed ceiling beams, a large island for cooking and eating, and a door to the private deck (with outdoor dining and grill). The bottom floor has 2 bedrooms (1 full bed, 1 queen bed), a guest room (2 single pull out beds and a door to the garden), and 2 full bathrooms. The duplex is very well equipped with A/C, heat, washer/dryer, dishwasher, and SMART TV. There are also toys, books and a 10-foot trampoline (in garden) to keep your kids occupied!
